articleTitle: EEG-Based Intelligence Quotient Assessment Using 1D Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: Intelligence Quotient (IQ), a critical measure of cognitive ability, holds significant importance in assessing an individual's intellectual capabilities. Our study aims to introduce a novel approach that utilizes EEG signals for IQ classification. A 1D-Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model has been employed for classifying the IQ level of an individual into three categories, i.e., ‘Low’, ‘Average’, and ‘High’. Overall, the proposed 1D CNN model is 95.86% accurate.

articleTitle: Metasurface-Integrated Flexible Antenna with Enhanced Bandwidth for Wearable IoT Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: This paper describes a novel technique for wearable IoT applications that integrates the metasurface with flexible antenna. The antenna combines the functionalities of metasurface technology with the mechanical flexibility needed for wearable devices. The antenna comprises a 4×4 array metasurface and a rectangular patch utilizing U-shaped and circular slots on wool substrates. The design achieves a 3.29 GHz wide bandwidth (5.97 GHz- 9.26 GHz) and a 5.2 dBi realized gain. The enhanced bandwidth has been employed to improve data transmission and reception of the wearable devices.

articleTitle: FSIR: Few-Shot Speaker Identification using Reptile Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: Speaker identification (SI) is the evolving biometrics and holds great potential for real-world applications. SI is challenging task with limited data in forensics. Few-shot learning inspires from human learning. In this work, SI tasks are investigated using optimization based meta-learning. A novel architecture for SI system is proposed and is based on a convolutional recurrent neural network. The accuracy is improved by 3% using the proposed framework, outperforming statistical methods.

articleTitle: Planar Insert Loaded Triple Band Waveguide Band-Pass Filter
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: This paper presents a light weight second order triple band waveguide band pass filter using planar insert technology. To achieve second order filter characteristics two identical planar insert in which resonators has been designed is inserted into the transverse plane of WR-90 rectangular waveguide at a distance of 8.41mm. The numerical analysis has been done using CST microwave studio, which shows center frequencies of 8.89/ 9.87/ 11.37 GHz, 3-dB bandwidth is 0.32/0.367/0.48GHz and insertion loss of 0.9/0.9/0.7dB respectively.

articleTitle: Low-Frequency Observation of Taurus-A with Signal Processing Techniques in Passive Mode Operation of CU-ST Radar
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: Calcutta University Stratosphere Troposphere Radar is a Pulse Doppler Active Phased Array of 473 Yagi-Uda Antennas at central frequency of 53 MHZ with a bandwidth of 8 MHz, arranged almost as a circular array. The facility under the University of Calcutta is located in Kalyani, West Bengal, India. It is a monostatic radar, devised to work primarily in active mode in atmospheric, ionospheric, and weather studies. And passive mode operation though supported by the system, involved various signal processing techniques and plotting methods. Passive mode is very lucrative considering no power being transmitted which reduces operational costs for Active Arrays. This paper outlines the steps involved in the radar operation and data processing in passive mode observation of astronomical source Taurus-A (see Table. 1), also known as 3C 144 or the Crab Nebula, on 18th April, 2023. It serves as a proof of concept as well as serves to understand its beam pointing accuracy and beam pattern.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning Approach for Position Control of a Mobile Robot
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: The study presents an innovative method for decoding the brain signals of subjects to control a Khepera IV mobile robot, thereby providing assistance to those with neuro-motor disorders. The afore-said objective is accomplished through a novel Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) that precisely classifies four motor imagination labels (left hand, right hand, left leg, and right leg) corresponding to four Khepera robot maneuvers (left, right, forward, and backward).

articleTitle: Smart Garden Sensor Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: Energy reusability and conservation of resources are a primary focus in today’s world. The proposed system uses Internet of Things (IoT) to harness natural resources and develop a smart garden maintenance system. Renewable energy sources like solar energy is used to power an automated robotic car that can trim excess grass in a garden. The robotic car is custom trained to detect grass and nearby objects using TensorFlow lite and OpenCV libraries. It can also estimate the distance of obstacles in its vicinity to avoid collisions. Water conservation is accomplished by rainwater harvesting and using the rainwater to maintain soil moisture level of the garden.

articleTitle: Design of Reconfigurable Metasurface for Beam Steering Applications in Next Generation Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: Metasurface designs can be classified as an emerging class of two-dimensional periodic sub-wavelength structures, those can manipulate the reflected phase of electromagnetic waves in such a manner, that conventional optics cannot. These surfaces are composed of arrays of subwavelength scatterers that interact with incident electromagnetic waves, allowing for complex manipulation of the wavefront. In this paper, a reconfigurable metasurface design is proposed, using varactor diode elements to manipulate the local reflection phase which can be utilized for beam-tilting operations in the desired direction. The unit cell is designed to operate in the Ka-band of frequencies, making it suitable for a wide range of operations in next gen communications. Also, the design highlights a two-dimensional beam tilt ability, which offers higher degrees of freedom for robust and real-time operations.

articleTitle: An Energy Efficient RSU Operating Scheme for 5G Enabled Intelligent Vehicular Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: Smart controlling of Roadside Unit (RSU) is possible by predicting urban traffic to minimize network resource consumption by enhancing energy efficiency in a great extent without interrupting the service. Suitable traffic prediction helps central controller to change dynamically the RSU status from standby to active mode as switch off and on mode. Performance evaluation exhibits the effectiveness of such RSU based intelligent transportation system (ITS).

articleTitle: Design and Testing of 2-kW TRM for a VHF Active Phased Array ST Radar at University of Calcutta
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: This paper describes the design and performance evaluation of a 2-kW solid state power amplifier (SSPA) based Transmit - Receive Module (TRM), operating at 53 MHz with maximum duty ratio of 5 % used in the University of Calcutta Stratosphere – Troposphere (ST) Radar system. The TRM design consists of different sections and a major 2-stage cascaded power amplifiers section in the transmit path. The testing involves the peak RF power output of the TRM and with different pulse widths. The TRM is tested for harmonics/spurious response, rise time, fall time and shape of the pulse spectrum.

articleTitle: Building Multihop LoRa Network for Enhanced Range and Quality Transmission of Healthcare Data
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: Efforts towards a cheap yet efficient health care infrastructure for remote rural areas requires longrange remote sensing communication over large areas. However, establishing efficient healthcare infrastructure in remote areas in developing countries like India, continues to be hampered by the lack of cost-effective and scalable IoT solutions. In this paper, a technique of multihop LoRa Network is built using relay for quality health data transmission for low-cost low power solution.

articleTitle: Hardware Prototyping of Handwritten Character Recognition using VEGA Soft Core Processor
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: In this paper, we propose the design and implementation of a hardware prototype system to recognise handwritten English alphabets using a multi-layer perceptron network (MLP). The proposed system is based on the indigenous soft core VEGA processor, which runs on a field programmable gate array (FPGA). The system is able to accurately recognise upper and lower case English alphabets. A detailed analysis of the system architecture and hardware is also presented.

articleTitle: Investigation of the DC Performance Characteristics of AlGaN/AlN/GaN nano-HEMT on β-Ga2O3 Substrate with a Graded AlGaN Buffer
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: In this paper, a recessed and field-plated gate AlGaN/AlN/GaN HEMT on β-Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> substrate using a graded AlGaN buffer layer is presented. The DC performance of proposed graded AlGaN buffer HEMT is investigated and compared with a conventional AlGaN/GaN HEMT of having without graded buffer. The findings exhibited that the graded buffer HEMT performed significantly better than normal HEMT in terms of transconductance, pinched-off, subthreshold behavior, and DC characteristics.

articleTitle: A Penta-Band Planar Horn antenna with Fan-shaped Beam Pattern
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: A substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) based H-plane horn antenna with fan-shaped beam pattern has been proposed for Ku and K-band applications. Three SIW-based H-plane horn antennas are joined judicially such that each arm makes an angle of 120° with the other arm to cover entire 360°. The entire structure is fed at the center using simple coaxial feeding method to excite the horn. The antenna shows a pentaband characteristic with operating bands across 16.13-16.24 GHz, 17.59-17.75 GHz, 19.37-19.64 GHz, 21.03-21.31 GHz, and 22.91-23.19 GHz, with a peak gain of 5.91 dBi at 21.17 GHz.

articleTitle: System Performance Analysis of High Throughput Satellites with On-Board Precoding
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: Precoding is an interference cancellation technique which enables aggressive frequency reuse in multibeam satellites thereby increasing the overall system throughput. This paper presents system level trade-off analysis for multibeam high throughput satellites (HTS) which use on-board precoding (OBP). The throughput performance is analysed for a 16-beam Ku band HTS, with and without precoding under different frequency reuse schemes. The payload mass and DC power requirements are also estimated to understand the penalties associated with its on-board implementation as compared to a conventional non-processing HTS.

articleTitle: Sensitivity Enhancement of TMD MOSFET-Based Biosensor by Optimization of Back Gate Parameters and Noise Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: In this work, a monolayer, dielectric-modulated (DM), double gate (DG), Transition Metal Dichalcogenide (TMD) Field-effect transistor (FET)-based Biosensor including the effect of back gate oxide parameter to assess the sensitivity of the proposed biosensor in a noisy environment is designed and simulated using SILVACO TCAD. Optimization of the device is achieved by modulating the back gate bias and back gate oxide thickness (BOX) to enhance the sensitivity. The proposed biosensor shows ~ 125% higher sensitivity with a back gate oxide thickness of 10 nm compared with sensitivity at a back gate oxide thickness of 200 nm at a back gate bias of V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">bg</inf>=−0.5 V. The Signal to Noise ratio (SNR) for the proposed biosensor is approximately three orders enhanced when compared to SNR of contemporary state-of-the-art Si-MOSFET-based biosensors.

articleTitle: Effect of Grooving Angle on Analog Performance of InGaSb Quantum Well p-MOSFET
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: We investigate the effect of the grooving angle on the analog performance of InGaSb-based quantum well p-MOSFET with raised source/drain architecture having a channel length of 14 nm and thickness of 5 nm with the grooving angle varying from 40° to 90°. Our study reveals that except for transconductance, the device with a narrower groove angle shows considerable improvement in all other analog parameters compared to the one with a broader groove angle.

Author Keywords: transconductance efficiency factor and voltage gain

articleTitle: Resource-aware Integration of Online Testing and Residue Removal for Cyber-Physical P-DMFBs
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: Paper-based Digital Microfluidic Biochips (P-DMFBs) have emerged as reliable, low-cost, and prompt-responsive platforms for biochemical assays. Reliability of P-DMFBs can be affected severely by physical defects introducing multiple faults, which even affect correctness of the outcome, cause sample-reagent wastage, and misuse resources. Therefore, testing is imperative during assay execution. Here, we propose an online testing strategy for cyber-physical P-DMFBs to ensure safe assay outcome in a limited-resource environment.

articleTitle: On Transmission Time of a LoRa Packet in a LoRa-Based IoT System for Underground Environment
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: Long range (LoRa) technology offers a potential solution for building internet of things (IoT) networks for underground environments. Offering large coverage distance with low power consumption is the key feature of the LoRa network that has been exploited in designing IoT network for underground environments. But a trade-off exists between the coverage distance and the transmission time of the LoRa packet that must be considered, otherwise, the performance of the LoRa network may be degraded. LoRa network supports variable spreading factor (SF) which controls the network performance such as coverage distance, transmission time, data rate etc. The present work presents a simulated study on the transmission time of the LoRa packet with variable SF. The study is important in designing the LoRa-based IoT network with desired coverage distance and network delay for the underground environment.

articleTitle: A Novel Design of an UWB PIFA Array Antenna for Medical Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: This work depicts a novel design of an array of two element Planar inverted-F antenna intended for biomedical applications in ISM band. The simulated result of the designed antenna exhibits high impedance matching with 47.33% impedance bandwidth and a peak gain of 2.53 dB. The proposed antenna may have a potential application as a biosensor for real-time glucose monitoring. Different concentration of glucose in blood when in contact of the proposed antenna, impacts the dielectric properties and induce a relative change in its resonant frequency.

articleTitle: Composite Split-Ring Shaped Slotted SIW cavity-backed antenna with Multilayer FSS as Superstrate for Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: A low profile circular SIW based cavity-backed antenna with Complementary Split Ring - shaped slot is designed at 5.33 GHz with a narrow bandwidth of 10 MHz. Studies are performed to obtain S11 and gain leading to values of -25 dB and 2.7 dBi respectively. Gain is augmented to 6.2 dBi on placing a multi-layer FSS over the antenna. A comparative study on composite antenna-FSS structure is performed followed by fabrication.

articleTitle: Influence of Interface Trap on Sensitivity of Doping-Less MoTe2 Hydrogen Sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: Hydrogen sensors based on two-dimensional (2D) materials have gained significant attention due to exceptional sensitivity, promising prospects for applications in gas detection and monitoring. This paper investigates the interplay between interface traps and sensor sensitivity in a doping-less like molybdenum ditelluride (MoTe2) hydrogen sensor. Through NEGF simulation we show that the presence of interface traps at the junction between the 2D material and the oxide impact the overall sensor behavior.

articleTitle: Experiment on spectrogram feature based CNN for sound anomaly detection
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: This work proposes an anomaly detection method for sound signals observed from motor shaft rotation. From the recorded sound data, time frequency spectrogram image feature is extracted and convolutional neural network (CNN) technique is used to detect change in the sound data pattern. The proposed method is implemented on a prototype edge device and experiments on real-time motor sounds show that classification accuracy of anomaly sound is 83.23%, 80.56%, and 78.44% for three types of noises - babble, music, and factory, respectively at 6 dB SNR. According to this study, the CNN technique outperforms other classical support vector machine (SVM) and k-nearest neighbour (KNN) techniques by 16.62% and 24.15%, respectively.

articleTitle: Localization Phase Transition in Quasi-Periodically Modulated Long-range Coupled Multicore Fiber
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: In this paper, we delve into the characteristics of the localization phase transition in a quasi-periodically modulated, long-range coupled multicore fiber. Our investigation reveals that the dependence of localization phase transitions on modulation strength significantly deviates from its behaviour in the planar counterpart. Moreover, for a fixed number of cores, the overall localization remains independent of the core arrangement radius and second next neighbour coupling (long-range) once a critical modulation strength is reached. Based on the study it is seen that even in scenarios of low modulation strength where long-range coupling is effective, we do not observe any signatures of reentrant delocalization with increasing of number of cores attributed to cyclic boundary effects.

articleTitle: Predictable Optical Performance of GeSn based p-i-n DBH cavity resonator
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: The aim of the present paper is to investigate the optical analysis of GeSn based p-i-n DBH cavity resonator. The optical gain and loss coefficient are estimated and compared with existing p-i-n cavity resonator. The effects of different loss mechanisms like free carrier absorption, different scattering processes, intervalley absorption have been considered for this analysis.

articleTitle: A D-Band Homogeneous Plano-Convex Lens Antenna with a Dual-Mode Conical Feed Horn
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: This manuscript reports the design of a linearly polarized homogeneous plano-convex lens antenna that operates at D-band. It is fed with a dual-mode conical horn to ascertain high polarization purity. The feed produces wide impedance bandwidth of ≈ 37% and about 15.7 dBi of gain at 140 GHz with half power beamwidths of 32° x 32° and cross polar discrimination (XPD) of about 55 dB. The overall lens antenna exhibits gain of about 40 dBi with 3dB beamwidths of ~ 1.4° x 1.4°.

articleTitle: Wearable Health Monitoring: Challenges and Opportunities
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: With the advent of wearable biomedical sensors and edge computing using low power microcontrollers, ambulatory health monitoring systems have been revolutionized over the last decade. Typical applications include cardiac arrhythmia detection, heart rate measurement and respiration tracking. The system consists of miniature biomedical sensors connected to a low power microcontroller which continuously analyzes the signals for prediction of abnormal events and also streams the data to a handheld device or IoT-enabled gateway for data archiving. The primary design considerations of these systems are energy consumption, form factor, complexity of abnormality detection and communication. Electrocardiogram (ECG), galvanic skin response (GSR) and photoplethysmogram (PPG) have been the principal sensing modalities of these systems. The embedded computing flow consists of signal quality assessment, filtering, features extraction and prediction (either abnormality, or a new parameter). Since resource constrained hardware is used, there should be an optimization between the desired detection accuracy and complexity of the detection algorithm. Data compression over the communication link can further enhance the energy efficiency of the overall system. This article provides a brief snapshot of wearable health monitoring systems with special emphasis on one-device computing.

articleTitle: A Low-Profile Microstrip Patch Array Antenna with Reduced Side Lobes
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a low-profile reduced side lobe microstrip patch array antenna at C band. It conceives a 4x4 array fed with a corporate feed network with non-uniform power distribution. The antenna produces a gain of about 16.5 dBi with half-power beamwidths of about 20°x20°. It exhibits side lobes about 20 dB lower than the main lobe.

articleTitle: Experimental Demonstration of Delay Compensation in Polarization Splitter Rotator on GF Fotonix Platform
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: We demonstrate a technique to compensate the differential group delay in a Polarization Splitter Rotator element. An extra waveguide length has been added in the TM-TE arm to mitigate the delay at the receiver. Experiments show that 5.2 ps delay posed by one Polarization Splitter Rotator is reduced to <1 ps.

articleTitle: A Handoff Algorithm For Dense Femto Cellular Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: In 5G network, femto cells are deployed alongside macrocell base stations. In a dense femto-cellular network scenarios, existing handoff algorithms cannot be implemented efficiently. The goal of this paper is i) to propose a handoff algorithm for dense femto cellular networks, and ii) to assess the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm with that of a conventional handoff algorithm under different instances of 5G network scenarios.

articleTitle: On Uplink Throughput Analysis for LEO Satellite Communications
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: In this paper, we analyze received throughput at the LEO satellite from the ground station, which would depend on transmission duration from the ground station as well as on the received power. Transmission duration is represented in terms of the satellite’s visible time, whereas the received power becomes a function of slant range and hence the elevation angle. Numerical results are shown at the end for different parameters’ values.

articleTitle: Impact of Cap Length in InAlAs/InGaAs Based High Electron Mobility Transistor
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: In this paper, a comparative study of the analog performance of InP-based High Electron Mobility Transistors (HEMTs) is conducted with varying cap lengths in the InAlAs/InGaAs hetero-structure. The study focuses on several key parameters, including ON current, transconductance, output conductance, intrinsic gain, ON-resistance, and ON to OFF current ratio. Our findings reveal that as the cap length increases, there is a noticeable improvement in the overall transistor performance.

articleTitle: Broadband Sub-50 GHz Microstrip Patch Antenna for 5G wireless Application
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: This work proposes a broadband (32.18 – 49.4 GHz) miniaturized (4.5 mm × 5 mm × 1.588 mm) antenna for sub-50 GHz 5G wireless applications. Slots are optimally placed on the radiating patch and ground of the Rectangular Microstrip Patch Antenna (RMPA) to achieve broadband characteristics. With a highest gain of 5.5 dBi at 41 GHz, proposed antenna exhibits 17.22 GHz wider impedance bandwidth and percentage bandwidth having 42.2%.

articleTitle: Polarization-Insensitive Tunable UWB Metasurface Absorber with Wide-Angle Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: An ultra-wideband, polarization-insensitive, graphene-based metasurface absorber has been proposed. The absorber provides absorptivity (A(f)) ≥ 90% from 0.1 to 5 THz, corresponding to 192.15% fractional bandwidth. In addition, metasurface also provides A(f) ≥ 80% for a wide-incidence angle (θ up to 60°) under both transverse electric and transverse magnetic polarizations. An increment in the chemical potential (μ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf>) from 0.2 to 0.7 eV leads to the blue shift in the absorptivity.

articleTitle: Smart Connected Future with Millimeter Waves: Challenges and Technology Directions
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: The convergence of communication and sensing with AI, security, high-performance computing, human-machine interfaces, is creating new technological paradigms. The advent of new applications calls for complex wireless channels with intelligence and flexibility enabling instantaneous exchange of information. This presentation discusses next generation multi-modal connected future use cases and addresses the millimeter wave challenges, prospects and technology directions.

Author Keywords: millimeter waves for connected future with intelligence

articleTitle: Modulating the Excitonic Emission from WS2 Nanostructures by Manipulating the Intrinsic Structural Defects and Extrinsic Impurity Defects
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: The Transition Metal Dichalcogenide (TMD), WS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, is a semiconducting 2D material with promising applications in optoelectronics and spintronics. Two strongly pronounced resonances, A and B excitons, are the main characteristics of the optical spectra of TMDs. The application of 2D TMD material in photonics is largely rooted in its potential to enable capabilities for engineering their exciton dynamics. In this paper, we discussed modulating the population ratio of A and B excitons in hydrothermally synthesized WS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> by manipulating the intrinsic structural defects and extrinsic impurity defects. Post-synthesis processing, like mild annealing, was employed to control the intrinsic structural defects of the TMD material, which ct as non-radiative channels for exciton relaxation. Further, substitutional doping with a p-type impurity (Vanadium) was employed to increase the free hole density in the valence band, thereby affecting the exciton emission.

articleTitle: Structural and Thermal Analysis of a Modular 1U CubeSat for RFI Survey on LEO orbit
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: In today’s space exploration, CubeSats are the preferred choice due to their functionality, cost, and time efficiency. The harsh environment of space exposes them to extreme conditions. In this paper, we analyze the CubeSat’s structure and thermal properties and develop a comprehensive model to predict its behavior. In this study, two CubeSat designs are compared showing the importance of load distribution.

articleTitle: Improvement of Isolation in UWB MIMO Antennas with Fractal and Hybrid-Fractal Structures
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: The paper suggests the numerical shaping and exploration of a miniaturized coplanar waveguide (CPW) fed 2-element ultra-wideband multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna including fractal and hybrid fractal structures for improvement of wideband isolation as well as attainment of triple band rejection characteristics. The radiator owns a wide impedance bandwidth extending from 3.4-12 GHz with an isolation above 15 dB. The radiator demonstrates high diversity traits accompanying steady gain and omnidirectional patterns. The possession of preferable impedance, radiation, and diversity traits thus allows the utilization of the radiator in portable UWB MIMO mobile terminals.

articleTitle: CMOS Based Ultra Low Power GRN Circuit Design for Bacterial Cell
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: Modeling of GRNs in low power electronic domain is an emerging approach towards bioelectronics device design. This study focuses on the analysis of transcription factors responsible for gene regulation in E.coli by using Cadence tool. Notably, our investigation observes hysteresis nature within the E.coli regulatory system with feedback loops and cooperative interactions. These findings are further validated by cell culture data, as reported in existing scientific literature.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Multi-Modal Data Fusion for Car Crash Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: This research introduces a deep learning model approach to enhance predictive modeling by fusing tabular and image data to improve car crash detection performance. Effectively integrating these diverse data types can significantly improve model accuracy. Using an ensemble technique, we propose an architecture that blends convolutional neural networks for images and recurrent neural networks for tabular data. Analysis performance on a real dataset showcasing its superiority over conventional single-modal models.

articleTitle: Noise Analysis of Bandgap Reference Circuit
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: This paper presents noise analysis of a Bandgap Reference Circuit which has an accuracy of 5.87 ppm/°C over the range of 0°C to 70 °C in 180nm technology. Special focus is given to the derivation of gain equations of each component and the noise spectral density of these components. Additionally, the paper conducts a comparative study of noise spectral density between single-stage and second-stage differential amplifier with respect to output voltage.

articleTitle: Estimation of Rain Attenuation from Effective Rain Rate calculations over a Tropical Location
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: The present study proposes a mathematical model that utilizes ground rain rate measurements to estimate a factor, called the effective rain rate, which in turn can be utilized to obtain the path-integrated rain attenuation at various Indian tropical locations in a more reliable manner compared to ITU-R at Ka-band frequencies and high rain rates prevalent in the tropical region.

articleTitle: A Comparative study of MOS characteristics with HfO2, ZrO2 and La2O3 as the gate dielectrics on Si substrates
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: The current work reports fabrication of MOS devices with high-K dielectrics for post- Moore integrated circuits. Such dielectrics are deposited using RF- sputtering technique. The equivalent oxide thickness of HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, ZrO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and La<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> are maintained to be 2.4 nm. The capacitance-voltage measurement indicates that the fixed-oxide charge is least for HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> followed by La<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and ZrO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. The leakage current is also least for HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and all the devices do not show any breakdown even after a constant voltage stress for 5000 seconds. Further, the shift in flat-band voltage under a constant voltage stress is also least for HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. Therefore, the current work compares the performance of different high-K dielectrics on Si substrates.

articleTitle: A Method of Dynamic Small Cell Deployment in 5G Two-Tier HetNet for Improved Area Spectral Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: In this paper, we present a cluster evaluation method to determine the optimal small cell density (SeNBs) in a 5G two-tier HetNet distributed through spatially clustered Non-Homogeneous Poisson Point Process (NHPPP). Incorporation of SeNBs is observed for Area Spectral Efficiency (ASE). Analytical results revealed that SeNBs with optimal density can improve the ASE in a HetNet even in peak hours considering urban tele-traffic distribution scenarios.

articleTitle: Orographic Rainfall Prediction by Soft Computing-A Comparison of Machine Learning and Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: The work attempts to compare Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) algorithm for a stochasticdeterministic orographic rainfall prediction. Comparing the prediction by Random Forest (RF), ML method and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) DL method it is found that for the forecasting purpose machine learning performs well with interrelated multivariate stochastic available input. However, DL can be used as powerful model for the nowcasting purpose even in case of absence of some related climatic input also for the short-term forecast purpose of hill orographic rain and obtained close to accurate prediction may be used for appropriate warning to avoid societal disaster.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Real-Time Lunar Terrain Detection for Autonomous Landing Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: Space exploration and research have led to many advancements in launch vehicles, landers, and rovers. Conducting in-situ observations requires identifying a safe landing location. To choose a safe landing site, this paper discusses computer vision technology for landers. This study utilizes the YOLOv5n model to identify the moon’s terrains. It is observed in this study that an accuracy of 92% can be achieved with near realtime detection using AI-edge devices.

articleTitle: Statistical Analysis of an On-Chip Low Power Current Source Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: The paper entails creating a low-power current reference circuit that uses a Beta Multiplier circuit to provide a constant PTAT(proportional to absolute temperature) current of 1nA. The circuit runs in the weak inversion area and lacks a resistor, instead employing three parallel PMOS with optimized W/L values. Monte Carlo analysis is used to investigate the performance of the circuit in relation to process parameters and threshold voltage. To predict the current value, a machine learning model utilizing Support Vector Regressor (SVR) is created, and its accuracy is measured by comparing the predicted values to the actual values using mean squared error. The goal of our work is to design an efficient low-power circuit that can be used in a variety of analog and mixed-mode systems.

articleTitle: Comparative Study among Various Machine Learning Algorithms towards the Detection of Alzheimer’s Disease
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: This article makes an attempt to make a comparative study among various machine learning algorithms in identifying dementia using some biomarkers inside the human brain. In connection to this, percentage volume of cerebro-spinal-fluid and lateral-ventricle are taken into consideration because of their drastic change with the severity of dementia in patients. A number of performance parameters has been computed in order to make a comparative study amongst various algorithms.

articleTitle: A Triple-Port MIMO Dielectric Resonator Antenna with Spatially Uncorrelated Pattern
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: This paper presents a design for a triple-port dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) tailored for WLAN applications, featuring a multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) configuration. The antenna system comprises a cylindrical dielectric resonator antenna (cDRA) and a ring dielectric resonator antenna (ri-DRA). To drive the cDRA, a pair of microstrip line-fed conformal striplines is employed, oriented orthogonally to ensure the excitation of the HE11δ mode. Notably, the proposed approach introduces an additional layer of complexity by exciting a TM01δ mode within the ring DRA. These two distinct dielectric resonator antennas operate in different modes, yielding two spatially uncorrelated radiation patterns. The combined implementation of these techniques results in remarkable port isolation exceeding 17 dB.

articleTitle: Plasmonic Biosensor by Using Different Shape of Grating Structures
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: Self referenced SPR based bio-sensor for different shape of grating structure with an average spectral sensitivity 700nm/RIU designed by TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> grating on thin gold (Au) film are of important research study in optical communication band. The COMSOL Multiphysics analysis has been performed to study the behavior of plasmon modes (analyte mode and substrate mode) at respective resonance conditions. The different shape of grating structure and the analytical results of sensitivity are also presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Novel Power Outage Probability Estimation Method for Energy Harvesting in Underlay D2D Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: Interference generated in beyond-5G device-to-device (D2D) networks can be utilized for ambient energy harvesting (EH) purposes to extend the lifetime of IoT devices. In this regard, power outage probability (POP) is an essential parameter for sustainability analysis in EH systems. This work presents a Gaussian mixture models (GMM)-based approach for POP estimation. The proposed approach provides a faster and more tractable and accurate measure of POP as indicated via numerical results.

articleTitle: A Wide Angularly Stabile Metasurface-based Band Pass Filter in Ka Band
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: In this report, a metasurface-based band-pass filter (BPF) operating between 30.3 GHz and 31.9 GHz with a fractional bandwidth of 5.2%, has been proposed for the Ka band application. Four concentric copper rings are arranged in a unit cell designed on top of an RT 6010 substrate with the completely etched backside. The unit cell dimension is 0.17λ × 0.17λ × 0.0036λ (at 31 GHz) with insertion loss 1 dB while the out of band response falls below 40 dB. The BPF shows angular stability up to 70°.

articleTitle: Design of a Brain-Actuated 2-Loop Position Control of a Robot Arm for Neuro-Motor Rehabilitation
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: The paper provides a brain-actuated position-control scheme of a robot-arm as a rehabilitative aid for people with acquired neuro-motor disability. Existing controllers employed for similar applications suffer from large steady-state error and settling-time, and high cognitive load. A 2-loop control system is proposed here to overcome the above limitations. Stability-analysis of the proposed system imposes a restriction on the maximum initial velocity of the robot-arm to maintain high stability.

articleTitle: Initial Observation of a Tropical Convection Event Using VHF Active Phased Array Main Radar of Calcutta University
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: Troposphere-stratosphere coupling mechanisms are significantly influenced by mesoscale convective events that are linked to severe weather. When a convection event passed over the radar station, winds, turbulence and layered structures are seen using a VHF radar at the tropical to sub-tropical transition location (22.58N, 88.38E geographic) in India. Radar-observed signal-to-noise ratio cross-sections for height and time showing height and time structures of increased air turbulence linked to the convection.

articleTitle: Enhanced photo-responsive behavior of MoS2 micro-flowers by Ag-doping
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: The two-dimensional material MoS2 is a promising candidate as a next-generation optoelectronic device. Pristine and Ag-doped MoS2 micro-flowers are synthesized by hydrothermal method. Both the samples show photoresponse at room temperature. Ag-doped MoS2 shows better photoresponse compared to undoped one. The highest responsivity obtained for Ag-MoS2 is found to be around 4.3 Amp/Watt which is more than three times the value for the undoped sample. The response time for the undoped sample is 0.6 s and Ag-MoS2 is 0.9 s.

articleTitle: An Approach to Compact Modeling of Organic Field Effect Transistor Using Bias-Dependent Parasitic Resistance
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: In this paper, a simplified model for bias-dependent parasitic channel resistance has been proposed to include in compact modeling of organic field effect transistor (OFET). Using the developed model, the drain current of the OFET is computed by iteration method and is verified with experimental data taken from literature for validation of the model. Results are shown for the effect of channel dimensions on the drain current and transconductance taking pentacene-based OFET as an example. Results may serve as a guide to the choice of channel dimensions to meet the target performance.

articleTitle: Dual wide band Cylindrical Dielectric Resonator Antenna integrated on Defected Ground Structure
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: This communication reports dual band cylindrical dielectric resonator antenna(DRA) based on defected ground structure. Two operating bands are achieved while the dielectric resonator is placed above defected ground structure. The novelty of this integrated DRA is that it offers dual wideband. The -10 dB impedance bandwidths are 2.54 GHz and 3.3 GHz at operating frequency 7.2 Ghz and 17. 7 GHz. The realised gain is 5 dBi and 8 dBi at resonance frequencies 7.2 GHz and 17.7GHz respectively. This antenna will work on X-and Ku-band. This antenna can be used in Satellite and Rader application. Efficiencies at both the bands are more than 95%. The proposed antenna has been designed and simulated by Ansys HFSS Software.

articleTitle: Design of Compact Multiband Circular SIW Cavity-Backed Slot Antenna for mm-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: This work presents a multiband circular SIW antenna for mm-Wave applications. This compact single-layer antenna comprises a circular SIW cavity and a radiating annular ring slot on the upper layer fed by an off-centered coaxial probe. The annular slot resonates at 32.4 GHz, 37.6 GHz, and 40.6 GHz providing triple-band characteristics. This miniaturized antenna provides a very good gain and radiation efficiency at all frequencies in the FR2 operational range.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Ge1-zSnz alloy-based Gate Underlap SiGe-Pocket DG-TFET
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: This article proposes a Ge<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-z</inf>Sn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">z</inf> alloy-based n-channel, dual material, double gate stack oxide TFET having a SiGe source pocket (n-type) and an underlap oxide at the gate-drain interface. The stack oxide includes SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> as the gate dielectric. This is seen to minimize the idle current whereas the SiGe source pocket and the Ge-Sn alloy as channel material, significantly increases the ON current. The ON current of the device obtained at V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">D</inf>=1V and V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">GS</inf>=1V is high (of the range ~10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup>A/μm). The incorporation of underlap oxide at the drain node of the channel greatly reduces the ambipolarity which is a major drawback of a TFET device.

articleTitle: Investigating the Impact of Grain Boundary Width on Average Grain Size in Nanoscale Polycrystalline Microstructures: A Multi-Phase Field and Finite Element Simulation Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: Phase field technique is an extremely versatile method capable to simulate intricate changes related to quenching of polycrystalline microstructures and the scope of its application has expanded to encompass a broad spectrum such as laser-based additive manufacturing, solidification, fracture, and more. In this study, we investigate the influence of gradient energy coefficients (k = 0.01 and k = 0.1) on the average grain size of a nanoscale polycrystalline microstructure using the multi-phase field method and finite-element technique for simulation.

articleTitle: An Improved Marker Beacon Receiver System
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: This work presents the integration of a RF front-end and baseband receiver components, operating at 75 MHz, into a marker beacon receiver system. A novel RF-IF architecture enhances the receiver RF selectivity to at least 37 dB at 75 MHz ± 10 kHz, and more than 22 dB audio channel isolation. The measured dynamic range without a fail is - 85 dBm to 0 dBm of RF input power. Further, the system employs a μ-processor for improved noise immunity. The complete architecture and measurement results are presented here.

articleTitle: Ppb-level NH3 Sensing Utilizing MoS2 Nanoflowers Towards Developing Exhaled-Breath based Point-of-Care Diagnosis of Chronic Kidney Diseases
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: This study explores the potential of detecting renal failure and chronic kidney diseases (CKD) by analyzing elevated ammonia (NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) levels in exhaled breath, offering a non-invasive, point-of-care diagnostic approach. Healthy individuals exhibit NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> levels between 50 and 1500 ppb in exhaled breath, whereas those with renal dysfunction display concentrations from 1500 to 15000 ppb. The research develops a cost-effective, rapid-response NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> sensor using MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanoflowers, demonstrating impressive performance with a response magnitude (RM) of around 40% at 100 ppm NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and a response time of 92 seconds. It also achieves a limit of detection (LoD) at 100 ppb NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>, with an RM of approximately 5% and a response time of 37 seconds. Even in humid conditions (95% relative humidity), the sensor maintains its limit of detection (LoD), making it a valuable tool for early diagnosis. This work addresses the pressing need for renal disease detection and showcases the potential of Transition Metal Dichalcogenide (TMDC) materials for cost-effective, non-invasive NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> sensing.

articleTitle: Cytomorphic Study of Smokeless Tobacco Induced Apoptosis in Neuronal Cells
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: Various cellular stress levels leads to p53 protein-regulated cell survival actions. Apoptosis, the programmed cell death, depends on the severity of stress level. Present study investigates the effect of Smokeless Tobacco (SLT) on neuronal cells and resulting Apoptosis process as the recovery mechanism. Here, we have mathematically modeled the Apoptosis pathway and simulated in Matlab platform. The simulated output validates the existing experimental works with Pearson’s correlation factor of 0.936.

articleTitle: Wideband Moderate Gain Dielectric Rod Antenna with Low Cross Polarization
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: This manuscript reports a simple technique to develop a linearly polarized dielectric rod antenna at 26 GHz. The basic antenna is designed theoretically. The design optimization is carried out using commercially available finite element method (FEM) based 3D electromagnetic solver. The antenna is designed considering Teflon (ε<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> = 2.08) as the dielectric material. The antenna is then fabricated using optimized dimensions. Antenna performance is measured in a Compact Antenna Test Range. The antenna produces wide impedance bandwidth of approximately 46% and a gain of about 14.8 dBi at 26 GHz. Its half power beamwidths are 32.2° x 34° and cross-polar discrimination (XPD) is higher than 28 dB.

articleTitle: Performance Enhancement of Armchair Graphene Nanoribbon Based Resonant Tunneling Diode Using Single-side Slanted Potential Well
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: The current investigation reports a new technique of slanting one side-wall of the potential well of an armchair graphene nanoribbon (AGNR) based resonant tunneling diode (RTD) structure to enhance its peak current (Ip) and negative differential resistance (NDR) region. Non-equilibrium Green’s function (NEGF) formalism has been used to study the structure. The proposed technique increases the peak current, negative resistance region, and peak-to-valley current ratio (PVR) of the conventional graphene based square well RTD structure. By suitably modulating the well width and barrier width of the RTD structure, its performance can be tuned over a wide range.

articleTitle: Tri-axial Patch antenna array configuration for Direction of Arrival (DoA) application
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: This paper shows analysis of a tri-axial patch antenna array resonant at ~2.4 GHz and assesses its performance for Snapshot-averaged MPM based DoA (SAM-DoA). SAM-DoA is a source localization technique designed for three orthogonal linear antennas. In our study, we examine the linearity of the patch antenna and its behavior in response to plane-wave excitation using CST antenna design simulation software. Designed traxial patch antenna exhibits good linearity and response.

articleTitle: Image transmission in underwater acoustic communication channel using LDPC codes
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: Traditional methods in underwater acoustic communication (UWAC) often struggle to overcome signal degradation and noise interference. This paper explores the application of low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes for improved image transmission in UWAC. The proposed work demonstrates the efficacy of a rate six by seven and a rate five by six LDPC codes in the UWAC channel to compensate the variable nature of noises in UWAC.

articleTitle: Reflectivity Measurement of Sand at W band using FMCW RADAR
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: The reflectivity of sand is measured at W band comparing the returned signal from sand and flat metal surface. FMCW RADAR based system at W band is designed, simulated and realized to build the measurement set up. Measured reflectivity matches closely with the theoretical results.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Analysis of Dynamic and Hybrid CMOS Threshold Logic Based Full Adder Circuit
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: Researchers have proposed various CMOS based full adder circuits. Here a new hybrid CMOS TLG design of full adder is presented using Ganged CMOS and COWL (Capacitive output wired Logic) based Threshold Logic Gate. Full adder circuit has been also designed here using two dynamic CMOS based TLG. One is dynamic capacitive output wired logic and another one is CMOS capacitor coupling logic (C3L). The performance parameters of the various TLG based full adder circuits were compared and the hybrid CMOS TLG based full adder circuit showed the best performance.

articleTitle: Ensemble Machine Learning model for Ionospheric TEC Prediction over Low-Latitude Regions
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: Predicting ionospheric TEC enhances GPS and NavIC navigation by countering solar and magnetic field effects. We introduced an ensemble of Random Forest, AdaBoost and XgBoost for TEC prediction in central India’s low-latitude region. Equatorial Ionization Anomaly makes low-latitude TEC forecasting challenging. Our novel work is to make an ensemble modelling algorithm for strengthening and improved performance.This approach not only capitalizes on the unique strengths of each algorithm but also produces a combination effect that enhances the overall performance. It is possible to utilize TEC gradients from Radio Interferometers like GMRT to reconstruct smaller-scale changes using these models [1].

articleTitle: A Compact Single Layer Dual-Bandstop Frequency Selective Surface for WLAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: In this paper, the design of a compact single-layer frequency-selective surface (FSS) is discussed. The unit cell of this proposed FSS structure is composed of a modified interconnected open square-headed dumbbell-shaped (OSHD) structure located at the four corners. This unique configuration imparts dual-bandstop characteristics to the FSS, resulting in stopband behavior spanning bandwidths of 230 MHz and 300 MHz, with resonant frequencies of 2.4 GHz and 5.0 GHz, respectively. To illustrate the bandstop behavior, surface current distribution and electric field variations are discussed. The unit-cell size of this FSS is 0.12λ0, where λ0 represents the free-space wavelength at the lower resonant frequency. Notably, the proposed FSS exhibits polarization independence and maintains stable performance upto 60% for both Transverse Electric (TE) and Transverse Magnetic (TM) polarizations. The design and analysis of this structure were carried out using the ANSYS HFSS software.

articleTitle: An intelligent field-effect transistor biosensor for ultrasensitive real-time biomolecule detection
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: Various attempts to achieve real-time ultrasensitive detection of biomolecules has been limited due to significantly overlapping data in the low concentration range. Herein we report and validate graphene field-effect transistor biosensor coupled with signal processing unit for ultrasensitive serotonin detection in real-time mode. The data processing algorithm captures multiple features from transient response of the sensor to classify an unknown sample and predict presence or absence of serotonin for unknown sample.

articleTitle: A Novel Methodology for Dynamic Thresholding Technique under Varying Illumination Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: This research introduces a new dynamic thresholding method, designed for changing illumination conditions in image processing. Traditional fixed thresholds struggle with varying light due to factors like voltage changes, LED aging, etc. The proposed technique adapts thresholds using background image intensity as a reference, employing a supervised approach with polynomial curve fitting via Python's numpy library. This innovative dynamic thresholding, combining supervised learning, enhances object detection and segmentation in machine vision systems, aiding tasks like foreign matter removal in tea, grain quality monitoring, etc.

articleTitle: In Search of Lunar Water at Northern Hemisphere
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: Longitudinal-latitudinal profile of surface number density distribution of lunar water (atomic mass unit 18) for mid-latitude to high-latitude/polar region has been studied for the first time for sunlit lunar exosphere during the pre-sunrise, day, sunset and midnight using the CHACE II on board Chandrayan-2 for northern hemisphere of Moon. Diurnal variation of relative abundance of water in terms of surface number density indicates pre-sunrise enhancement as per theoretical expectation. The quantitative validation of number density shows a substantial amount of water reserve at the lunar surface at high and mid latitude. There is a clear indication of shifting of water towards the poles has been found which is in line with previous Chandrayaan missions and LADEE mission results.

articleTitle: Digitally Controlled RF Beam-Forming system at X Band for Estimation of Direction of Arrival
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: A digitally controlled radio frequency (RF) beam forming receiver is designed, simulated and realized at X band frequency for estimation of direction of arrival (DOA). A sixteen element linear array is fabricated for demonstration where the phase and amplitude of each array element can be digitally controlled to steer the beam in any desired direction within ±50 deg to get the DOA of the target.

articleTitle: A Ku-Band Power Amplifier MMIC For Space Application
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: This paper describes a Ku-band power amplifier (PA) monolithic microwave integrated circuit (MMIC), designed using space qualified 0.13µm GaAs pHEMT foundry process from M/s OMMIC. The MMIC can be used for the development of beacon SSPA and for driver stages of high power SSPAs at Ku-band frequency for on-board applications. The MMIC is a two stage amplifier in balanced configuration yielding higher RF power, moderate gain and fully matched 50 Ohm input and output impedances over wide-band. It demonstrates a small signal gain of better than 20 dB in the frequency range of 10.4 – 12.4 GHz and delivers better than 30 dBm (1W) saturated output power with power added efficiency (PAE) of 21% at center frequency for a chip size of 4.15 X 3.5 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Maturity Level Detection of Banana Fruit by Image Processing Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: The assessment of fruit ripeness is a critical task in various agricultural and food processing applications. Traditional methods of ripeness evaluation, which relied on human judgment, were subjective and labor-intensive. In this paper, a comprehensive approach is presented for fruit ripeness detection of banana using image processing technique. An algorithm was developed in MATLAB for finding different image components of banana sample and fundamental parameters like the number of yellow and white pixels.

articleTitle: A Low-Profile, Dual-Band Frequency Reconfigurable Antenna for 5G/WLAN/Wi-MAX Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: In this paper, a PIN diode is employed for frequency reconfiguration. An antenna is operating between 2.57 - 3.52 GHz and 4.89 - 6.18 GHz, it suits Wi-MAX (3.3 GHz), WLAN (5030 - 5990 MHz), and n46 (5150 - 5925 MHz) 5G bands when the diode is ON, and WLAN/n46 bands when OFF. The antenna achieves over 85% radiation efficiency and favorable gain, establishing it as a strong contender for 5G/WLAN/Wi-MAX applications.

articleTitle: A Novel Machine Learning Based Fall Detection System using Acclerometer and Gyroscope
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: Falls are regarded as a very serious problem for the majority of elderly individuals. In this study, a prototype of a machine learning-based fall detection system is developed. In the developed system, an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) is used to detect different types of falls, namely, ‘falling forward’, ‘falling right’, ‘falling left’, ‘falling backward’, and ‘no fall’ (standing, walking, sitting) using the data received from 3-axis accelerometer and gyroscopic sensor.

articleTitle: OFDM On-Off Keying Index Modulation (OFDM-OOK-IM) with Enhanced Spectral Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: The proposed On-Off Keying-based OFDM-IM (OFDM-OOK-IM) technique indirectly conveys the significant number of data bits, as OOK-index bits, apart from the constellation data, resulting in improved Spectral Efficiency (SE) and Electrical Efficiency compared to its counterpart techniques with reduced end-user complexity in practice by avoiding the indexing using a lookup table. At the receiver, threshold detection is used, followed by a customised log-likelihood ratio (LLR) detection algorithm. SE comparison of contemporary IM schemes confirms the superiority of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Concept study of UV coverage of Radio interferometry in space using small satellites
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: Space Very Long Baseline Interferometry (SVLBI) revolutionizes astronomy using multiple satellites for enhanced resolution and sensitivity. This paper analyzes u-v distribution in Space VLBI (SVLBI) with varying satellite numbers and orbits. It explores changes in u-v coverage with identical and diverse orbits. Configurations featuring diverse inclinations, eccentricities, and apogee heights show promise for effective u-v coverage, generating redundant baselines and enhancing data calibration, benefiting low-frequency radio studies like 21cm line.

articleTitle: A 12 GHz 17.5 dB Gain 0.8 dB NF Cascode LNA in 130 nm CMOS for Satellite Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: This paper reports a 12 GHz cascode LNA with extremely low noise figure (NF) for satellite communication (SATCOM) applications. The NF of the proposed LNA is improved by employing optimum transistor sizing, a high-Q gate inductor, and efficient use of an inter-stage matching inductor between the common source (CS) and the common gate (CG) transistor. Overall, the designed LNA achieves a gain of 17.5 dB, NF of 0.8 dB, and input third-order intermodulation coefficient (IIP3) of −12.5 dBm at 12 GHz with only 11.4 mW of DC power.

articleTitle: Design of an Optical sensor to detect Anaemia based on 2D Photonic crystal
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: Design of an optical biosensor based on 2D photonic crystals has been proposed in this paper. The sole purpose of the biosensor is to detect the presence of anaemia in infants who fall in the age group of 6 to 59 months. The proposed biosensor is able to detect mild, moderate and severe cases of anaemia. Simulation results indicate the creation of different defect states with increase in the severity of the disease and this will help in biosensing.

articleTitle: Optical Distributions in Dual-Core Surface Plasmon Resonance Sensor with Dual Coating of Metal and Metal Oxide Suitable for Sensing Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: In this paper, a dual core photonic crystal fiber (PCF) sensor has been designed in the near infrared region around 1.55 µm to 1.85 µm. The preliminary result of optical distributions such as core mode, plasmonic mode, resonance condition and dispersion relations of core mode and SPP mode of refractive index 1.36 is studied. Silver (Ag) is taken as the plasmonic material which is deposited outside the fiber structure to detect changes of the surrounding medium’s refractive index.

articleTitle: Time-Frequency Domain Speech Enhancement Framework using Audio Spectrogram Transformer with Masked Multi-head Attention
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: Speech enhancement is crucial in various applications, such as speech recognition, hearing aids, and telecommunications-VoIP. This paper presents a novel time-frequency domain speech enhancement framework utilizing an Audio Spectrogram Transformer (AST) with a Masked Multi-head Attention (MMHAt) layer. The AST is a convolution-free deep learning architecture, and it is directly applied to an audio spectrogram. Its multi-head attention layer can capture the long-range global context in the time-frequency domain. Moreover, the masking has been applied to ensure the causality of the Multi-Head Attention mechanism, which is essential for real-time applications.

articleTitle: VLSI Architecture of High Throughput Processing Unit for Efficiently Executing 2D Convolution for Deep Neural Network based Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: Convolution serves as a foundational component enabling Deep Neural Networks (DNN) to extract meaningful features from input data. This paper focuses on the real-time architecture of a high-throughput processing unit (PU) designed for 2D convolutions. Three distinct PU topologies are presented: (a) a non-pipelined Multiply-Accumulate (MAC) based PU, (b) a 2-stage pipelined MAC based PU, and (c) a 5-stage pipelined MAC-based PU, which significantly reduces convolution process delay. These proposed architectures are implemented on Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs) using the Xilinx Vivado tool. Resource utilization and latency are thoroughly assessed and compared across various PU topologies on Artix-7 and Zynq-7 FPGA chips. Additionally, throughput is estimated and compared for different kernel and image sizes, revealing a substantial average improvement of 96.36% achieved by the pipelined MAC with its five-stage design compared to the non-pipelined MAC-based processing unit.

articleTitle: Cooperative Beam Placement for Regional Non-GSO Satellite Communication Constellations
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: This paper presents a cooperative beam placement algorithm for non-GSO communication constellations with regional coverage. The number of beams required to be formed by each satellite are minimized by utilizing the inter-satellite coverage overlap and cooperative beam-planning. The efficacy of proposed algorithm is demonstrated through case study of an equatorial low earth orbit (LEO) constellation having northern Indian Ocean region coverage, where the number of beams per satellite for cooperative beam placement is compared with conventional fixed-beam method.

articleTitle: Exploration of Depth Perception in Human Binocular Vision using EEG-Based Neuro-Fuzzy Classifier
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: The paper proposes an innovative approach for assessing individual differences in depth perception within binocular vision, employing an EEG induced Neuro-fuzzy classifier. The study classifies depth perception into three levels (high, medium and low), leveraging alpha power activity acquired from occipital, parietal, and prefrontal brain lobes. The present research holds significant implications for various domains, including aviation, surgery, and clinical diagnostics.

articleTitle: Semi- Circular Ring slotted Circular Patch Antenna for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: A semi-circular ring slotted circular patch antenna has been designed in this manuscript at 3.7 GHz. The proposed 5G antenna has realized gain of 5.23 dBi at 3.7 GHz. This antenna is radiating over 3.67 GHz to 3.72 GHz. Therefore, the proposed antenna can be utilized for sub-6 GHz 5G applications. The fabricated antenna is tuned to 3.65 GHz and radiated over 3.62 GHz to 3.66 GHz.

articleTitle: Compact Waveguide Packaging of High Power Transmitter at W band
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: In this paper a W band transmitter front-end with continuous wave (CW) power output has been realized in a compact waveguide package. Two MMIC namely a multiplier and power amplifier (PA) has been integrated in a multichip module in a waveguide package size of 40.3 mm X 43 mm X 22.3 mm which can provide output power of 21.2 dBm.

articleTitle: Radial Basis Function Method for Linearization of Thermocouple Data: An Efficient and Accurate Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: This research paper proposes a novel approach for the linearization of non-linear thermocouple data using the Radial Basis Function (RBF) method. The proposed approach utilizes a different RBF function with author-defined hyperparameters to map the non-linear relationship between temperature and voltage to a linear one. The linearized data is then passed through a linear function for further refinement. The performance of the proposed approach is evaluated using various metrics such as accuracy, linearity percentage, loss, and error percentage. The results show that the RBF method is an efficient and accurate approach for the linearization of nonlinear thermocouple data. This research paper contributes to the field of thermocouple data analysis by introducing a new method that can improve the accuracy and efficiency of thermocouple measurements.

articleTitle: Super Junction GaN HEMT: Achieving High Breakdown Voltage and Low Harmonic Distortion
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: This study explores the impact of varying the super junction length (L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SJ</inf>) on ON current, ON resistance, transconductance, and breakdown voltage. Additionally, attention is directed toward the device’s linearity and harmonic distortion, crucial for reliability assurance. The goal is to comprehend the effects of changes L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SJ</inf> on device traits, enabling targeted performance optimization in AlGaN/GaN Super junction HEMTs for specific applications.

articleTitle: Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Broadcast Using Satellite over Indian Air Space
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Broadcast (ADS-B) is an aircraft surveillance technology in which a transmitter is placed in top and bottom of aircraft and broadcasts surveillance data such as position, velocity & aircraft identification to nearby aircraft ground stations. It can also reach to the spacecraft present in line-of-sight of the broadcasting aircraft. The paper outlines the approach to estimate the satellite antenna gain requirement in space-based ADS-B with an objective to meet Indian air space coverage requirement and its distribution statistics. The simulation uses aircraft ADS-B antenna pattern to provide optimum results over different elevation angle. The simulation results also derive the optimum geostationary orbital location to meet service requirement.

articleTitle: Performance Study of ZnO/SnO Thin Film Heterojunction Solar Cell
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: The interesting properties of both Tin monoxide (SnO) and Zinc Oxide (ZnO) semiconductors allow to predict promising photovoltaic performance of n-ZnO/p-SnO heterojunction. In this work, one-dimensional numerical simulation is used to study and optimize the n-ZnO/p-SnO thin film based heterojunction solar cell. The effects of ZnO and SnO thickness on the performance of ZnO/SnO heterojunction solar cell is investigated. A highest efficiency of 15.85% is obtained for ~1.75-2.0 μm of SnO absorber layer thickness.

articleTitle: Point of Care Diagnosis of Liver Fibrosis by Detecting the Responsible VOCs in Exhaled Breath using ZnO Homojunction Diode
publicationTitle: 2023 8th International Conference on Computers and Devices for Communication (CODEC)
abstract: In the present paper, Zinc Oxide (ZnO) homojunction based vapor sensor device was developed for point of care diagnosis of liver fibrosis by detection of the volatile organic compounds (VOCs) present in exhaled breath of the patient suffering from that disease. Among the various VOCs present in the exhaled breath, three vapor species act as potential biomarkers for detection of liver fibrosis namely acetone, ethanol and isopropanol (with acetone being the primary biomarker). Thus, to detect liver fibrosis through the exhaled breath, a cost-effective ZnO homojunction vapor sensor device was fabricated by depositing sol gel grown sodium (Na) doped thin film on top of ZnO nanotubes by dip coating method. The fabricated sensor displayed a good sensing performance towards acetone, ethanol and isopropanol with response magnitude of 24.9%, 7.3% and 4.1% respectively. The lowest limit detection achieved by the sensor device was 1 ppm for acetone vapor and 50 ppm for ethanol and isopropanol vapor. Such device was found to be successfully discriminate between a healthy person and a patient suffering from liver fibrosis.

articleTitle: Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia Classification using Compact Channel Specific Multi-column CNNs
